transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-28
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (CTO - ApexLytics), Maya Torres (Sr ML Engineer), Elena Rossi (Head of Data)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from our side, I'm Jordan, account exec at Redwood, and Priya's our solutions engineer. how about you all?
[00:12] Samir: Hi, Samir here. CTO at ApexLytics. we run the search service for our product search and support articles.
[00:17] Maya: Maya, I own the embeddings work and evals. delighted to meet you.
[00:22] Elena: Elena, Head of Data, want to understand compliance and residency implications.
[00:28] Jordan: Great, thanks. high-level we'll try to cover architecture, current pain points, target metrics, and then options — hosted, dedicated, or private — and what a pilot looks like.
[00:40] Priya: quick q — is your current stack fully elasticsearch-based for retrieval?
[00:45] Samir: yeah, ES with BM25 for recall and a homegrown ranker for final scoring. latency is okay but relevance for long-tail queries suffers. and our support articles search is noisy.
[00:56] Maya: we've experimented with OpenAI embeddings and a pinecone prototype but the cost and throughput were concerns. also indexing dimensionality was kind of ad-hoc, we used 1536 dims initially.
[01:12] Jordan: makes sense. for reranking workflows, a common pattern is BM25 for candidate generation then embeddings-based rerank — that reduces vector ops. curious what throughput you expect.
[01:22] Samir: target is around 2M queries/day peak with 99th percentile latency under 200ms for search surface, but for support article rerank we can accept up to 500ms.
[01:33] Priya: okay that's helpful. for 2M q/day—do you know what fraction will hit embeddings vs just BM25?
[01:40] Maya: roughly 60% will be product search (BM25 + rerank), 40% support (full-text + rerank). so embeddings ops maybe on 100-200 million vector lookups a day depending on batching.
[01:53] Jordan: that's where deployment mode matters. Hosted can handle that but costs scale; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and reserved capacity; Private/VPC helps if you need on-prem or strict residency.
[02:05] Elena: our compliance requirement — SOC 2 is mandatory, plus we use GCP KMS for key management. we may need logs for audits and data retention controls.
[02:15] Priya: Redwood supports SOC 2 and we integrate with customer KMS for private offerings; hosted uses Redwood-managed keys but we offer customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private. audit logs and retention configs are configurable.
[02:27] Samir: good. about vector DBs — we were leaning to Milvus because of cost but pinecone had better latency in our tests. thoughts?
[02:36] Priya: Milvus is good for self-hosted and scales, but managed Pinecone has optimized indexing and lower operational overhead. Redwood can route to your vector DB or we can host vectors in our runtime — we also support Redis vector or an S3-backed index for cold storage.
[02:51] Maya: routing to our Milvus cluster is interesting because we like to keep vectors in our VPC. would that work with Redwood Dedicated/Private?
[02:59] Priya: yes — for Dedicated, we can route calls to your VPC endpoints and keep data in your network; for Private deployments we can deploy the control plane in your VPC so vectors never leave your environment.
[03:09] Samir: latency and throughput: how does Redwood handle batching and KV cache for decoder-style rerankers?
[03:18] Priya: our runtime does continuous batching and has a KV cache to reduce repeated prefix work for chat workflows; for reranks it's lighter but we do vector query batching and prefetching. latency depends on model size and quantization — for dense rerank models we recommend 1536 or 1024 dims depending on model, and we can quantize to int8/4 for faster MLPs.
[03:36] Maya: dimensionality tradeoffs — we've seen 1536 gives better quality but increases storage and compute. any guidance?
[03:42] Jordan: typical tradeoff: 768-1024 hits a sweet spot for many open models; if you need higher quality on product names long tail, 1536 can help. Redwood's optimizer provides recommendations per eval set.
[03:53] Elena: what about hybrid search — BM25 + embeddings — do you support a combined ranking?
[03:58] Priya: yes, we often do hybrid: BM25 for candidate generation then embeddings similarity and finally a learned reranker/LLM for reorder. we provide tooling to test different cutoffs and recall/precision tradeoffs.
[04:12] Samir: measurement — we'll need to see real evals. can you run a benchmark on a subset of our catalog?
[04:18] Priya: absolutely. for benchmarks we need sample vectors, documents, and a target SLA. we'll run throughput tests with realistic QPS and provide token-level cost estimates.
[04:28] Maya: on cost, curious how Redwood charges for embeddings and rerank calls: per token, per embedding vector op?
[04:34] Jordan: hosted API is usage-based — per embedding unit and per-token for model calls; Dedicated has reserved capacity pricing. we'll share a pricing sheet but we can also model cost for your workload to compare hosted vs dedicated.
[04:48] Samir: security detail — do you support SAML/SSO and role-based access?
[04:53] Priya: yes, SSO with SCIM provisioning, RBAC, and per-route permissions. audit logs can be exported to your SIEM.
[05:02] Elena: data residency — our EEA customers require EU-only storage. can Redwood restrict regions?
[05:07] Jordan: yes, region pinning and private deployments in EU regions are supported. for Dedicated we can reserve capacity in a region.
[05:15] Maya: any gotchas with vector dimensionality when using Pinecone vs Milvus?
[05:19] Priya: Pinecone and Milvus both support various dims; Pinecone's managed service optimizes index types under the hood and can auto-tune, Milvus gives you more control but needs more ops. storage format and quantization differ — we can help pick index params for recall/latency tradeoffs.
[05:34] Samir: for the pilot let's plan 1 week of functional evals and 2 weeks of load testing?
[05:39] Priya: typically we do a 2-3 week pilot: initial setup and integration + 1 week of benchmarks. we can tune after measuring.
[05:47] Jordan: next steps recap in a sec. quick question on integration — do you want Redwood to manage embeddings and store vectors, or do you prefer to keep vectors in your Milvus?
[05:56] Maya: we prefer to keep vectors in our VPC, at least for the first pilot.
[06:01] Priya: that's fine. we'll provide an auth endpoint pattern and VPC peering options; for Dedicated we can do private connectivity.
[06:10] Samir: what about model versions and rollouts? we want a safe rollback if quality regresses.
[06:15] Priya: Redwood has rollout policies, canary deploys, A/B, and automatic fallback to cheaper variants. we also provide eval hooks to compare EER/precision on your prompts.
[06:26] Elena: compliance question again — how long are vectors persisted in hosted mode by default?
[06:31] Jordan: hosted retains vectors per policy; we can configure retention windows or purge on demand. for Dedicated/Private vectors live in your infra, so retention is under your control.
[06:42] Samir: curious about caching — do you have prefix caching for rerank model LLMs?
[06:47] Priya: KV cache is mostly for autoregressive generation; for reranker models which are usually bi-encoder + cross-encoder, caching helps at the encoder stage if the same doc embeddings are reused. we also support embedding cache for frequent queries.
[07:00] Maya: are there pre-built connectors to ES/Milvus?
[07:04] Priya: yes we have connectors and sample jobs for syncing embeddings into Milvus/ES, and utilities to keep embeddings fresh.
[07:12] Samir: SLA — what's typical 99th percentile for dedicated pods?
[07:17] Priya: Dedicated can target sub-100ms 99th for vector lookup-only flows, rerank with a cross-encoder will push latency higher depending on model. we size based on your QPS and target latency.
[07:30] Jordan: okay, I want to capture the pilot scope — Maya/Samir will provide 2 sample datasets (product catalog + support corpus) and target SLAs. Redwood will run a benchmark against those datasets, route to their Milvus via VPC, and produce a cost/latency recommendation and suggested embeddings dims.
[07:49] Elena: timeline on getting security docs?
[07:52] Jordan: I'll send SOC2 summary + KMS notes by Friday 2026-07-30.
[07:57] Maya: for the benchmark we'll need an idea of acceptable recall drop relative to current BM25 — say we target +X NDCG?
[08:04] Priya: we'll propose a few eval metrics and thresholds, but yes include the NDCG targets in the data you share.
[08:10] Samir: one more — are you able to do hybrid rerank that combines BM25 score and cosine similarity?
[08:16] Priya: yes, we support score blending and learned rankers that take BM25, embedding sim, and business signals.
[08:24] Jordan: wrapping up — next steps we listed. any final Qs?
[08:29] Elena: none from me.
[08:31] Maya: no, thanks.
[08:33] Samir: thanks, appreciate it.
[08:35] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the security pack and scheduling for the benchmark. talk soon.

End of meeting.

Notes on transcript quality: some product names transcribed (e.g., "pine-cone" vs Pinecone) and technical terms may be slightly off — typical Fireflies output.
